system: You are an expert reviewer of machine-learning research ideas.
user:
Compare two research ideas for the SAME research problem and pick the stronger one.

Research problem: In MVFA's few-shot inference, the released code min-max normalises the zero-shot (text) branch and the few-shot (memory-bank) branch with the minimum and maximum over the entire test set and adds them with a fixed weight of 0.5, so the score of one image depends on the rest of the test set and a single incoming image cannot be scored. Can this transductive normalisation be replaced by an inductive one computed only from the K normal support images, at a small cost in AUROC? The inductive normaliser maps each branch's patch scores through the 1st and 99th percentiles of the leave-one-out patch scores of the supports (every patch of support i scored against the memory bank of the other K-1 supports and against the text anchors), which gives thousands of reference values even at K = 2; the fusion weight and the max pooling of the image score are kept fixed. Primary outcome: image-level and pixel-level AUROC of inductive versus transductive normalisation on each held-out BMAD dataset for K in {2, 4, 8, 16}. Motivating measurement: the spread of the original method's AUROC across random half-size test subsets and at shifted prevalence (10% and 50% abnormal). Secondary outcome: sensitivity at 95% specificity with a threshold fixed from the support scores alone.

A stronger idea is one whose proposed change acts on the SPECIFIC mechanism of the target method that causes the problem (here: the released MVFA code and its verified behaviour), rather than a generic improvement that would apply to any anomaly detector.

Judge on:
1. Specificity. Would this idea plausibly solve THIS problem in THIS method better than a generic alternative? A mechanism that applies equally to any model and any problem is WEAKER, not stronger, because it does not explain why it fixes this problem.
2. Evidence. Is the proposed mechanism supported by the cited literature or by verified properties of the code and the benchmark?
3. Testability. Does the idea make a concrete, falsifiable prediction that can be checked on BMAD with one Colab GPU?

Explicitly DO NOT reward: length or polish of the write-up, stacking many modules, vague "add an attention/adapter module" proposals, or ideas that need data, labels or compute that are not available.

Idea A:
TITLE: Analytic zero-shot scale plus support CDF for the few-shot branch
SUMMARY: Normalise MVFA's zero-shot branch without any target data, from the anchor geometry and source-validation statistics, and only the few-shot branch from the K supports via a leave-one-out empirical CDF.
HYPOTHESIS: With the zero-shot branch normalised analytically and the few-shot branch by the support CDF, fused image AUROC stays within 1 point of the transductive pipeline at K >= 4, and at K = 2 it loses at least 1 point less than normalising both branches from the supports.
RATIONALE: The anchor-geometry parent shows that the zero-shot branch reads the anchors only through their difference, so its scale is a property of the trained model, not of the target. The CDF parent gives a robust support-based scale where target data are needed. A different allocation follows: the zero-shot branch needs no target statistics at all (its normaliser can be fixed on source validation), and the scarce K supports are spent only on the memory-bank branch, whose scale genuinely depends on the target. This halves the number of quantities estimated from K images.
METHOD: 1) calibrate_zero.py: on source validation splits, compute zero-shot patch projections on the unit anchor-difference direction per level; store median and MAD of normal patches. 2) test_few.py: zero-shot z = (proj - median_src)/MAD_src mapped by a logistic; few-shot via LOO empirical CDF of support scores; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. No adapter training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baselines: both branches by support CDF; both by support percentiles. Falsified if the hybrid is not better than both-support normalisation at K = 2.

Idea B:
TITLE: Position-wise leave-one-out empirical CDF with neighbourhood pooling
SUMMARY: Map each patch score through the empirical CDF of leave-one-out support scores from the same grid neighbourhood, mixed with the global support CDF according to how many reference values the neighbourhood holds.
HYPOTHESIS: At K >= 4 on spatially aligned held-out modalities, the position-wise empirical CDF improves pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over the global empirical CDF and keeps image AUROC within 1 point of the transductive pipeline, while every score stays exactly invariant to the test set.
RATIONALE: The empirical-CDF parent gives an assumption-free, test-set-invariant scale but ignores anatomy; the position-wise parent removes anatomy offsets but relies on mean/standard-deviation statistics from very few values. Their combination keeps the rank-based CDF and makes the reference set local: for position j the references are all LOO support patch scores within a 3x3 (level 4: 5x5) neighbourhood, and the local CDF is mixed with the global one with weight n_j/(n_j + 50).
METHOD: 1) utils.py: build_local_refs(support_maps, radius): sorted arrays per position; global array as in the parent. 2) cdf_mix(s, R_local, R_global) = w F_local(s) + (1 - w) F_global(s), w = n/(n + 50). 3) test_few.py: apply per branch and level, then 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: radius {1, 2}, mixing constant {10, 50, 200}. No training.
EXPERIMENT: Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: global empirical CDF. Metrics: image/pixel AUROC, sensitivity at 95% specificity. Falsified if the local CDF is not better than the global CDF in pixel AUROC on aligned modalities.

Respond in exactly this format:
REASONING: <one to three sentences explaining your choice>
CONFIDENCE: <HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW>
WINNER=<A | B | TIE>
response:
REASONING: Idea A directly addresses the specific root cause of the score-balancing failure in MVFA's dual-branch architecture: the two branches have fundamentally different statistical dependencies, where the text branch is target-invariant and governed by fixed anchor geometry while the few-shot branch depends on support data. By pre-calibrating the zero-shot scale and reserving scarce support statistics entirely for the memory-bank branch, Idea A specifically resolves the calibration mismatch at small $K$ without introducing spatial alignment assumptions that fail across unaligned medical modalities.
CONFIDENCE: HIGH
WINNER=A
